correctness.rationale: On each labelled K_{a,b,c} under simultaneous strict open-neighborhood majority with individual tie retention, a nonuniform shore in a periodic 2-orbit must be frozen: no update can recreate nonuniformity after a strict majority. One reversing shore is impossible. Exactly two reversing shores must be oppositely monochromatic and equal in size t; their fixed third shore of size c with h one-bits gives exactly C(c,h) solutions iff |2h-c|<t. With three reversing shores there is one orbit exactly when the maximal shore size is unique. These disjoint cases establish P_2=1_{unique largest}+sum_{i<j:n_i=n_j} sum_h C(n_k,h)1_{|2h-n_k|<n_i}, counted as UNORIENTED temporal 2-orbits, for every positive a,b,c. Direct independently written bitmask enumeration matched (1,1,1):0, (1,1,2):3, (1,1,4):7, (1,2,3):1, (2,2,3):7 and (2,2,2):6. Finite tests corroborate, not prove the universal classification.
